bib.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
bib.venue: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; proofs in Appendix G read but not re-derived.

question: Can a zeroth-order optimizer that needs only forward passes and inference-level memory fine-tune billion-parameter language models competitively with backpropagation?
hypothesis: With a task prompt and adequate pre-training, the loss landscape has low local effective rank, so ZO-SGD converges at a rate that depends on that rank rather than on the number of parameters, and so is not catastrophically slow.
contributions: In MeZO, we adapt the ZO-SGD algorithm [88] and a number of variants to operate in-place on arbitrarily large models with almost no memory overhead (see Algorithm 1 and Section 2).
Comprehensive experiments across masked and autoregressive LMs, 350M to 66B, on classification, multiple-choice and generation tasks; MeZO consistently outperforms zero-shot, ICL and linear probing.
Compatibility of MeZO with full-parameter tuning and PEFT (LoRA, prefix-tuning).
MeZO can optimize non-differentiable objectives such as accuracy or F1 at inference-level memory.
Theory: per-step rate (Theorem 1) and global convergence (Lemma 3) depend on local effective rank, not parameter count.

method.summary: MeZO is ZO-SGD with the SPSA two-point gradient estimator implemented in place: the Gaussian perturbation z is regenerated from a saved random seed instead of stored, so memory equals inference. It is applied to RoBERTa-large (k-shot) and OPT 13B/30B/66B (1000 training examples) with prompts, and compared to zero-shot, ICL, linear probing and Adam fine-tuning.
method.task: Fine-tuning pre-trained LMs for classification, multiple-choice and QA generation without backpropagation

datasets.name: SST-2, SST-5, TREC, MNLI, SNLI, RTE (RoBERTa-large)
datasets.size: k=16 or k=512 examples per class for both training and validation; test set limited to 1,000 examples
datasets.source: SST-2/SST-5 Socher 2013, TREC Voorhees 2000, MNLI Williams 2018, SNLI Bowman 2015, RTE (Dagan 2005 and successors); licence not stated
datasets.preprocessing: Prompt templates adapted from Gao et al. 2021 (Table 13)

datasets.name: SuperGLUE (BoolQ, CB, COPA, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, WiC, WSC) + SST-2 + SQuAD + DROP (OPT)
datasets.size: 1,000 train, 500 validation, 1,000 test, randomly sampled per dataset
datasets.source: SuperGLUE Wang 2019; SQuAD Rajpurkar 2016; DROP Dua 2019; licence not stated
datasets.preprocessing: Prompts from GPT-3 and PromptSource with minor changes (Table 14); SST-2 used for development

other.layers_note: inferred: 24 layers from 'RoBERTa-large has 24 + 2 = 26 parameter groups' (layers plus embedding and head)

models.name: MeZO (full, LoRA r=8 alpha=16, prefix m=5)
models.params: full-parameter; LoRA about 19M and prefix about 6M trainable on 66B

other.prefix_init: prefix initialised from keys and values of randomly sampled vocabulary tokens passed through the LLM; crucial for MeZO stability

training.objective: Classification: cross entropy on label-word logits (prompt-based, Gao 2021). Multiple choice and QA: teacher forcing on the correct candidate, loss only on candidate tokens. Non-differentiable variants: accuracy (RoBERTa) or F1 (SQuAD).
training.optimizer: MeZO = ZO-SGD with SPSA, n=1, Gaussian z; FT baseline uses Adam (SGD also reported); MeZO-Adam variant in Appendix
training.lr: MeZO RoBERTa {1e-5,1e-6,1e-7} (ablation grid) ; Table 15: MeZO lr {1e-7,1e-6,1e-5}, prefix {1e-2,5e-3,1e-3}, LoRA {1e-5,5e-5,1e-4}; OPT MeZO {1e-6,1e-7}, prefix {1e-2,1e-3}, LoRA {1e-4,5e-5} (SQuAD/DROP have a third value); FT Adam OPT {1e-5,5e-5,8e-5}
training.lr_schedule: MeZO: constant; FT with backprop: linear
training.warmup: none for MeZO (warmup gave identical results in ablation)
training.batch_size: MeZO RoBERTa 64; MeZO OPT 16; FT Adam OPT 8; FT RoBERTa {2,4,8} (k=16), {8,16,32} (k=512)
training.steps: MeZO: 100K steps (RoBERTa), 20K steps (OPT); FT: 1K steps (RoBERTa), 5 epochs = 625 steps (OPT)
training.weight_decay: 0 for MeZO and FT in general; 0.1 for MeZO (LoRA) on RoBERTa; all 0 for OPT
training.hardware: Nvidia A100 80GB (up to 16x A100 for full FT of 66B); NVLink and InfiniBand
training.compute: 30B MultiRC: MeZO takes 32x more steps than FT, FT takes 8x more GPUs and 7.74x more time per step; MeZO needs half the GPU-hours
training.seeds: Ablations (Appendix A): k=16 averaged over 5 seeds. Number of seeds for the main tables is not stated.

other.epsilon: RoBERTa MeZO 1e-3, prefix 1e-1, LoRA 1e-3; OPT MeZO 1e-3, prefix 1e-1, LoRA 1e-2
other.checkpointing: RoBERTa: validate every 1/10 of steps, keep best; OPT: every 1/5 of steps, keep best; 30B and 66B use last checkpoint only
other.ablation_budget: Algorithm ablations fixed at 10,000 forward passes on RoBERTa-large SST-2, SNLI, TREC, k=16; grid batch {16,64} x lr {1e-5,1e-6,1e-7} x eps {1e-3,1e-5} x wd {0,0.1}
other.storage: Checkpoint reconstructible from seed plus 20,000 steps x 2 bytes (<0.1MB for 66B)
other.linear_probing: classification: scipy linear classifier; multiple-choice and generation: head-tuning of LM head only, batch 8, lr {1e-4, 5e-4}, 5 epochs

inference.decoding: Greedy decoding for generation (SQuAD, DROP); classification and multiple-choice predict the candidate with highest average per-token log-likelihood
inference.samples: single run per cell in OPT tables; RoBERTa tables report mean (std) over seeds, count not stated
inference.prompting: Prompt-based fine-tuning is required; ICL baseline uses 32 examples in context

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: classification and multiple-choice accuracy on held-out test set

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: QA token F1 for SQuAD and DROP

metrics.name: Peak GPU memory
metrics.definition: nvidia-smi peak, per-device batch size 1, no gradient checkpointing; run counts as successful if no OOM for at least 100 steps

eval.protocol: RoBERTa-large k=16 and k=512, accuracy mean (std); OPT 1,000/500/1,000 split; best MeZO variant reported in Tables 2 and Fig 1

prompts.text:
<premise>
Does this mean that "<hypothesis>" is true? Yes or No?

evidence.quote: We run MeZO for 20K steps and fine-tuning for 5 epochs, or 625 steps
constant learning rate for all MeZO experiments

results.claim: On OPT-13B, MeZO (best of full/LoRA/prefix) matches or beats Adam fine-tuning within 1% on 7 of 11 tasks.
results.setup: OPT-13B, 1000 train examples, prompts, MeZO 20K steps vs FT Adam 5 epochs; best of three MeZO variants chosen per task (Fig 1)
results.quote: comparable (within 1%) or better performance than FT on 7 out of 11 tasks
results.note: Selection of best variant per task uses the test numbers in Table 1; plain MeZO alone is worse on some tasks (e.g. BoolQ 67.6 vs 73.8 LoRA).

results.claim: MeZO uses the same memory as zero-shot and up to 12x less than standard fine-tuning.
results.setup: OPT family on MultiRC (400 tokens average), A100 80GB, batch size 1 per device, no gradient checkpointing
results.quote: offering memory savings of up to 12 times compared to standard FT
results.note: Table 22: 13B MeZO 26GB vs full FT 316GB on 4xA100.

results.claim: On one A100 80GB, backprop with Adam fits only a 2.7B model whereas MeZO trains 30B.
results.quote: backpropagation with Adam is feasible only for a 2.7B LM

results.claim: MeZO needs 32x more steps than FT on OPT-30B yet only half the GPU-hours.
results.setup: OPT-30B, MultiRC; FT uses 8x GPUs and 7.74x more time per step; implementation-dependent
results.note: Main text steps: 20K MeZO vs 625 FT = 32x. RoBERTa: 100K vs 1K steps.

results.claim: MeZO has 7.74x faster per-step wall-clock than full FT on a 30B model.
results.setup: OPT-30B, MultiRC, 80GB A100 with NVLink/InfiniBand; MeZO 1 GPU 5.896s vs FT 8 GPUs 45.608s
results.quote: training with MeZO brings 7.74× speedup per step

results.claim: On CB (OPT-13B) plain MeZO is far behind FT.
results.setup: OPT-13B, 1000 train examples, full-parameter MeZO vs FT Adam
results.table: Table 1, row MeZO vs row FT (12x memory), column CB (67.9 vs 83.9)
results.note: MeZO (prefix) reaches 69.6 on CB, still 14.3 below FT.

results.claim: On MultiRC (OPT-13B) plain MeZO is 11 points behind FT.
results.setup: OPT-13B, 1000 train examples, full-parameter MeZO vs FT Adam
results.table: Table 1, row MeZO vs row FT (12x memory), column MultiRC (60.1 vs 71.1)

results.claim: RoBERTa-large with k=512, MeZO is within 5% of fine-tuning on all six tasks and beats linear probing.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large 350M, k=512 per class, prompts, MeZO 100K steps vs FT 1K steps
results.quote: the gap between MeZO and FT further reduced to within 5% across all tasks
results.note: Table 18 k=512: MNLI MeZO 78.3 vs FT 84.4 (6.1 points) and SNLI 83.0 vs 88.7 (5.7 points), so 'within 5%' is not an absolute-point gap for every task; the best MeZO variant (prefix) gives 79.8 and 84.8.

results.claim: Without a prompt MeZO fails: SST-2 drops to near chance.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large k=16, 10,000 forward-pass budget, 5 seeds; no-prompt grid extended with lr 1e-4
results.table: Table 5, row No Prompt vs row Prompt, column SST-2 (51.9 vs 89.6)

results.claim: Optimizing accuracy directly with MeZO works but is worse than cross entropy: TREC 68.6 vs 94.3.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large k=512, full-parameter MeZO optimizing accuracy vs MeZO cross entropy; zero-shot 32.0
results.table: Table 3, row Accuracy/F1 (MeZO) vs Cross entropy (MeZO), column TREC
results.note: SQuAD (OPT-13B, MeZO prefix, F1 objective, 1,000 examples): 78.5 vs 84.7 with cross entropy.

results.claim: Checkpoint storage for MeZO is a seed plus one scalar per step, under 0.1MB for 66B.
Forward-mode autodiff (JVP) needs 830.66 MB excess memory vs 327.50 MB for inference and 24,156.23 MB for backprop.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, JAX, batch size 16, MultiRC, model weights not counted
results.table: Table 12, row Excess Memory (MB), columns Inference (327.50), Backpropagation (24156.23), Forward Auto-Differentiation (830.66)

results.claim: The two-point SPSA estimator is much more efficient than a one-point estimator at equal forward passes.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large k=512; SPSA 20K steps vs one-point 40K steps (same forward-pass count)
results.table: Table 11, row SPSA 20K vs row One-point estimate 40K, column TREC (92.7 vs 73.0)

results.claim: MeZO beats gradient-free BBTv2 by up to 11 points absolute on RoBERTa-large.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large k=16; BBTv2 numbers taken from Sun et al.
results.note: Table 21 SNLI: MeZO prefix 71.6 vs BBTv2 57.3 (14.3), MeZO 68.5 (11.2).

results.claim: MeZO optimizes 66B models and beats zero-shot and ICL on most tasks, but 66B SQuAD with full MeZO failed without further tuning.
results.setup: OPT-66B, 1000 examples, best of MeZO and MeZO (prefix) vs ICL
results.table: Table 2, row 66B MeZO/MeZO (prefix), column SST-2 (93.6 vs ICL 89.3)
results.note: Table 20 marks 66B MeZO SQuAD with * : 'MeZO requires further tuning to successfully optimize.' 66B RTE MeZO 66.4 vs zero-shot 67.2.

results.claim: Convergence rate of ZO-SGD scales with local effective rank r, not parameter count d (Theorem 1, Lemma 3), versus a factor d from classical analysis (Lemma 2).
results.setup: Assumes local r-effective Hessian rank and PL inequality; gamma = Theta(r/n)
results.note: Theory rests on an assumption not verified for LLMs (authors say the Hessian rank is too costly to measure).

limits: MeZO takes many more steps (20K vs 625 for OPT; 100K vs 1K for RoBERTa) to reach comparable accuracy; the wall-clock win is implementation-dependent.
Only works with a task prompt; without one SST-2 falls to 51.9 (Table 5).
Gap to FT remains large on some tasks (CB, MultiRC, WIC) and 66B full MeZO on SQuAD did not train without further tuning.
Local effective rank assumption is not measured on LLMs; theory is for the idealised sphere/Gaussian z.
Non-differentiable objective results are preliminary, and cross entropy still wins (Table 3).
Not combined with FlashAttention, gradient checkpointing or quantization; memory comparisons exclude these.
Memory comparison uses batch size 1 per device and no gradient checkpointing, which favours MeZO.
Number of seeds for the main tables is not stated; OPT tables are single numbers with no variance.
Best variant of MeZO is selected per task on Fig 1 and Table 2, but 'best' is not described as validation-selected.

terms.definition: Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation: gradient estimate (L(theta+eps z; B) - L(theta-eps z; B)) / (2 eps) * z with z ~ N(0, I)
memory-efficient zeroth-order optimizer: ZO-SGD that regenerates z from a saved seed to operate in place with inference-level memory
tr(H)/||H||_op of a Hessian upper bound H in a neighbourhood of the iterate is at most r

code.snippet: projected_grad = (l_plus - l_minus) / (2*eps); theta_i <- theta_i - eta_t * projected_grad * z, with z regenerated from seed s
